[[File:Hudson Riv WW stone SE JC jeh.jpg|right|thumb|Walkway adjacent to Liberty National Golf Course]]
The '''Hudson River Waterfront Walkway''', also known as the '''Hudson River Walkway''', is a promenade along the [[Hudson Waterfront]] in [[New Jersey]]. The ongoing and incomplete project located on [[Kill van Kull]] and the western shore of [[Upper New York Bay]] and the [[North River (Hudson River)|Hudson River]] was implemented as part of a New Jersey state-mandated master plan to connect the municipalities from the [[Bayonne Bridge]] to the [[George Washington Bridge]] with an urban [[linear park]] and provide contiguous unhindered access to the water's edge.

There is no projected date for its completion, though large segments have been built or incorporated into it since its inception.<ref name="kelly">{{cite web | last = Kelly| first = Mike | title = Hudson River Walkway is far from finished | work =  The Record| date = October 16, 2008 | url = http://www.northjersey.com/environment/Kelly_Hudson_River_Walkway_is_far_from_finished.html | access-date = 2009-02-23}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Hortillosa, Summer Dawn|url=http://www.nj.com/hobokennow/index.ssf/2011/09/photos_hudson_river_walkway_to.html|title=PHOTOS: Hudson River Walkway tour to showcase waterfront's beauty, history|publisher=[[NJ.com]]|date=September 13, 2011|access-date=March 19, 2022|archive-date=October 18, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018131010/http://www.nj.com/hobokennow/index.ssf/2011/09/photos_hudson_river_walkway_to.html}}</ref> The southern end in [[Bayonne, New Jersey|Bayonne]] may eventually connect to the [[Hackensack RiverWalk]], another proposed walkway along [[Newark Bay]] and [[Hackensack River]] on the west side of the [[Hudson County]] peninsula,<ref>{{Cite web|author=McDonald, Corey W.|date=2016-12-20|title=Waterfront walkway around Hudson County slowly but surely progressing|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2016/12/hudson_river_walkway_sees_progress_but_years_until.html|access-date=2021-03-13|website=NJ.com|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126034041/https://www.nj.com/hudson/2016/12/hudson_river_walkway_sees_progress_but_years_until.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and form part of a proposed Harbor Ring around the harbor. Its northern end is in [[Palisades Interstate Park]], allowing users to continue along the river bank and alpine paths to the New Jersey/[[New York (state)|New York]] state line and beyond. (A connection to the [[Long Path]], a {{convert|330|mi|km|adj=on}} hiking trail with terminus near [[Albany, New York|Albany]], is feasible.)

As of 2007, {{convert|11|mi|km|spell=in}} of walkway have been completed, with an additional {{convert|5|mi|km|spell=in}} designated HRWW along Broadway in Bayonne. A part of the [[East Coast Greenway]], or ECG, a project to create a nearly {{convert|3000|mi|km|adj=on}} urban path linking the major cities along the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic]] coast runs [[Concurrency (road)|concurrent]] with the HRWW.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.libertygap.org/hudson-guide.html |title=HRWW and East Coast Greenway |website=Liberty Water Gap Trail |access-date=September 16, 2011 |archive-date=October 6, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006081405/http://www.libertygap.org/hudson-guide.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.greenway.org/pdf/nj_map.pdf |title=East Coast Greenway |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927035307/http://www.greenway.org/pdf/nj_map.pdf |archive-date=2011-09-27 |publisher=Vanasse Hangen Brustlin, Inc. |access-date=September 16, 2011}}</ref>

In 2013 the walkway showed signs of age. Some of the [[piling]]s on which it is built succumbed to [[marine worm]]s and [[effects of Hurricane Sandy in New Jersey]], which undermined bedding.<ref>{{cite news|last = Hack|first = Charles|title = New Jersey Land Conservation Rally will address Hudson River waterfront today at NJIT|newspaper = The Jersey Journal|date = March 9, 2013|url = http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2013/03/new_jersey_land_conservation_r.html|access-date = 2013-03-10|archive-date = 2014-08-12|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140812052657/http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2013/03/new_jersey_land_conservation_r.html|url-status = live}}</ref>

==Route==
[[Image:Hudson River NASA.jpg|thumb|right|NASA image of the lower Hudson]]
The distance of the walkway from beginning to end is approximately {{convert|18.5|mi|km}} as "the crow flies". It is considerably longer as it follows the contour of the shoreline.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/08/15/realestate/a-river-walk-s-piecemeal-birth.html?src=pm | work=[[The New York Times]] | first=Dennis | last=Hevesi | title=A River Walk's Piecemeal Birth | date=August 15, 1999 | access-date=February 9, 2017 | archive-date=March 6, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306044619/http://www.nytimes.com/1999/08/15/realestate/a-river-walk-s-piecemeal-birth.html?src=pm | url-status=live }}</ref>

It traverses established residential and commercial areas, re-developed piers, wetland preservation zones, industrial and transportation infrastructure, and is dotted with public and private marinas and parks. Expansive views of the water and the New York skyline can be seen from most of its length. It passes through the following municipalities, which have combined population of approximately 545,000, as of the 2010 census.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=http://lwd.dol.state.nj.us/labor/lpa/census/2010/2010data/table7cm.xls |title=Table 7. Population for the Counties and Municipalities in New Jersey: 1990, 2000 and 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807100630/http://lwd.dol.state.nj.us/labor/lpa/census/2010/2010data/table7cm.xls |archive-date=2017-08-07 |publisher=[[New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development]] |date=February 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2021}}</ref>

==History==
A walkway or promenade along the northeastern New Jersey waterfront was first discussed at a state level in the late 1970s. In 1988, the [[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]] created the Coastal Zone Management Rules, which outlined the regulations and specifications for its construction. They require anyone building within {{convert|100|ft|m}} of the water's edge to provide a minimum of {{convert|30|ft|m}} wide open, public space along the shoreline. Construction must be permitted by the agency and paid for by the developer. In 1999, the [[National Association of Home Builders]] and the New Jersey Builders Association challenged the obligation in court as an unfair taking of private property under [[eminent domain]], saying that property owners should be compensated as specified by the "Takings clause" of the [[Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fifth Amendment]]. A federal judge rejected the suit, upholding a state rule that requires property owners to provide access to the waterfront.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9407E1D61738F93AA2575BC0A96F958260 |title=Judge Upholds Law on Waterfront Access |work=The New York Times |agency=Associated Press |date=August 19, 1999 |access-date=October 7, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | last = Hevesi|first = Dennis| title = A River Walk's Piecemeal Birth| work = The New York Times| date = August 15, 1999 | url = https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9900E7DD1439F936A2575BC0A96F958260 | access-date = 2009-02-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/voices/index.ssf/2011/03/daily_poll_do_you_believe_coas.html |title=Daily poll: Do you believe coastal access rules should be changed |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015055035/http://www.nj.com/hudson/voices/index.ssf/2011/03/daily_poll_do_you_believe_coas.html |archive-date=2012-10-15 |publisher=NJ.com |work=[[The Jersey Journal]] |date=March 24, 2011}}</ref> By the end of 2019, most of the Walkway was complete. Only seven "gaps" remain to be built from Liberty State Park in Jersey City to the George Washington Bridge. Major sections of the Walkway remain unbuilt in industrial Bayonne.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://jerseydigs.com/bayonne-plans-to-add-new-pedestrian-bridge-along-hudson-river/ | title=Bayonne Plans to Add New Pedestrian Bridge Along Hudson River | date=30 June 2021 | last=Fry | first=Chris | website=Jersey Digs | access-date=11 July 2022 | archive-date=11 July 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711022138/https://jerseydigs.com/bayonne-plans-to-add-new-pedestrian-bridge-along-hudson-river/ | url-status=live }}</ref>
